rules.name: Mandatory field control
rules.purpose: Protect the audit trail and make sure every billing line can be traced back to a customer, invoice, service and period.

rules.name: Expected amount present
rules.purpose: The automation cannot prove billing accuracy without a contract or pricing baseline.

rules.name: Billed amount present
rules.purpose: A blank billed amount blocks billing approval because no charge can be validated.

rules.name: Invalid amount control
rules.purpose: Negative amounts may create incorrect credits or revenue leakage unless approved as a credit-note process.

rules.name: Billing mismatch tolerance
rules.purpose: The core billing accuracy control compares expected contract value against the amount being invoiced.

rules.name: High billing mismatch
rules.purpose: Large billing differences require escalation before invoices are released to customers.

rules.name: Duplicate invoice control
rules.purpose: Duplicate invoice records can cause double billing and customer disputes.

rules.name: Contract end control
rules.purpose: A customer should not be billed after contract expiry unless renewal evidence exists.

rules.name: Inactive service control
rules.purpose: Cancelled, suspended or pending services should be reviewed before charging.

rules.name: Currency control
rules.purpose: The South African monthly billing run should be in ZAR unless routed through a separate foreign billing process.

rules.name: Billing period cut-off
rules.purpose: Invoice dates outside the billing period can distort revenue reporting and month-end controls.

rules.name: Usage anomaly review
rules.purpose: Large month-on-month spikes may be valid, but they need supporting usage evidence.
